trial_court: Second Additional District Judge, Hazaribagh - Matrimonial Suit No. 36 of 1993
case_name: Deepa Dutta @ Smt. Deepa Ghosh vs Pradeep Ghosh
facts_of_case: Marriage between Pradeep Ghosh and Deepa Dutta was solemnised on 19.11.1992. The husband alleged that the wife was insane at the time of marriage and concealing that fact. The suit was filed for annulment of the marriage under Section 11 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: A decree for divorce by mutual consent can be passed without going into the reasons of mal-adjustment in the marriage.
legal_principles.held: If only these three conditions are satisfied, it is obligatory on the part of the court to pass a decree for divorce without going into deep as to the reasons of mal-adjustment in the marriage or other reasons behind their living separately.

legal_principles.principle: The grounds for divorce and judicial separations in Hindu marriages are more stringent than those in Muslim or Christian marriages.
legal_principles.held: When there was no ground for divorce available under the Act but the circumstances could not be able to adjust themselves, there remained then no scope for getting the marriage annulled by a decree of divorce.

legal_principles.principle: The conception of Hindu marriage is sacramental, not contractual.
legal_principles.held: In Muslim and Christian marriages, the concept is of contractual one while the Hindu marriage is of sacramental.

legal_principles.principle: The three conditions for a decree of divorce by mutual consent are: (i) spouses living separately for more than one year, (ii) they have not been able to live together, and (iii) they have mutually agreed that the marriage should be dissolved.
legal_principles.held: Only three conditions are necessary for decree of divorce by mutual consent- (i) when the spouses are living separately for more than one year (ii) that they have not been able to live together (iii) that they have mutually agreed that the marriage should be dissolved.

outcome.final_order: The trial court's decree annulling the marriage was upheld.
